scenes.narration: Push a box and it speeds up; push harder and it speeds up more.
scenes.picture: A child's hands pushing a cardboard box across a smooth wooden floor, motion lines behind the box, bright classroom setting, no text

scenes.narration: The same push moves a heavy box more slowly than a light box.
scenes.math: same F, bigger m → smaller a
scenes.picture: Two identical cardboard boxes side by side, one light and empty, one filled with heavy books, a single hand pushing each, simple illustration, no text

scenes.narration: So acceleration grows with force and shrinks as mass grows.
scenes.picture: A simple balance scale comparing a small force arrow and a large mass block, clean flat illustration, soft blue background, no text

scenes.narration: Put together: acceleration equals force divided by mass.
scenes.picture: A glowing simple equation symbol made of three blank shapes connected by arrows, abstract science illustration, no text or symbols

scenes.narration: For example, ten newtons pushing two kilograms gives five metres per second squared.
scenes.math: F = 10 N, m = 2 kg → a = 5 m/s²
scenes.picture: A small cart on a track pushed by a hand, floating blank coloured discs representing force and mass, physics lab illustration, no text

scenes.narration: Try it: double the push on the same object and its acceleration doubles.
scenes.picture: A skateboard pushed by two hands instead of one, twice as many motion lines, cheerful cartoon style, no text
